title: OpenSSH 9.6p1 — CVE-2024-6387 (regreSSHion) RCE
description: OpenSSH 9.6p1 Ubuntu 3ubuntu13.18 falls within CVE-2024-6387 affected range (8.5p1<=9.7p1). Race condition in signal handler allows unauthenticated RCE.
risks: Unauthenticated remote code execution leading to full server compromise.
attack_vectors: Exploit race condition in sshd(8) signal handler during login. Requires multiple attempts (~6-8 hours avg). Attack must time SIGALRM handler between alarm() and setjmp().
proof_of_existence: PORT 22/tcp open ssh OpenSSH 9.6p1 Ubuntu 3ubuntu13.18 (Ubuntu Linux; protocol 2.0). CVE-2024-6387 affects 8.5p1 through 9.7p1.
remediation: Patch OpenSSH to 9.8p1 or later, or apply vendor backport patch for Ubuntu.

title: Weak SSH MAC algorithms (hmac-sha1) enabled
description: SSH server accepts hmac-sha1 and hmac-sha1-etm MAC algorithms, which use SHA-1 — a deprecated hash with known collision vulnerabilities.
risks: Weakened data integrity; potential for MAC downgrade attacks in MITM scenarios.
attack_vectors: MITM attacker could negotiate hmac-sha1 MAC during SSH session, weakening integrity guarantees. SHA-1 collisions enable forgery in theory.
proof_of_existence: mac_algorithms include: hmac-sha1-etm@openssh.com, hmac-sha1 alongside strong options like hmac-sha2-256, hmac-sha2-512.
remediation: Remove hmac-sha1 and hmac-sha1-etm from MACs in sshd_config; keep only sha2-256/512 and umac variants.

title: SSH password authentication enabled
description: SSH server accepts both publickey and password authentication methods. Password auth enables brute-force and credential stuffing attacks.
risks: Credential brute-force, password spraying, and credential stuffing attacks against exposed SSH service.
attack_vectors: Automated brute-force tools (hydra, medusa, ncrack) can attempt password authentication. Credential stuffing using leaked password databases.
proof_of_existence: ssh-auth-methods: Supported authentication methods: publickey, password
remediation: Disable PasswordAuthentication in sshd_config; use key-based auth only. Add fail2ban for additional protection.

title: CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' for scripts and styles
description: Content-Security-Policy header includes 'unsafe-inline' in both script-src and style-src directives, significantly weakening XSS protection.
risks: XSS attacks can inject inline scripts/styles, bypassing CSP protection. Reduces defense-in-depth against client-side attacks.
attack_vectors: Inject inline JavaScript via reflected/stored XSS. CSP will not block execution since 'unsafe-inline' is permitted in script-src.
remediation: Remove 'unsafe-inline'; use nonces or hashes for inline scripts/styles. Use Tailwind CDN via SRI or self-host.

title: No WAF detected on web services
description: nmap WAF detection scripts returned no WAF signature. Web services are directly exposed without WAF filtering layer.
risks: No automated protection against OWASP Top 10 attacks, bot traffic, or vulnerability exploitation attempts.
attack_vectors: Direct exploitation of web vulnerabilities without WAF interception. SQLi, XSS, path traversal attempts not filtered.
proof_of_existence: WAF detection scripts ran on ports 80/443 with no WAF fingerprint results returned.
remediation: Deploy a WAF (Cloudflare, ModSecurity, AWS WAF) in front of web services.

title: SSL/TLS configuration hardened — no vulnerabilities found
description: SSL/TLS properly configured: SSLv2/v3 and TLS 1.0/1.1 disabled, only TLS 1.2/1.3 enabled, not vulnerable to Heartbleed, strong ciphers only.
risks: No SSL/TLS-related risks identified. Configuration follows best practices.
attack_vectors: No viable SSL/TLS attack vectors identified.
proof_of_existence: SSLv2/v3/TLSv1.0/1.1 disabled. TLSv1.2/1.3 enabled. Not vulnerable to heartbleed. Strong ciphers: ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384.
remediation: No action needed. Maintain current SSL/TLS configuration.
